hints.content:
$f$ is decreasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $f(x)$ decreases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going downwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals f of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, twenty-four and the x-intercept negative four, zero. It continues to decrease until the local minimum at negative three, negative eight. Then it increases through the x-intercept negative one, zero until the local maximum zero, four. Then it decreases through the x-intercept one, zero, the point two, negative twenty, and the point three, negative fifty-five. All values are approximations. the function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative three and after x equals zero.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $f$ decreasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-2<x<-1.5$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is increasing on this interval
$-1<x<0$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is increasing on this interval
$0<x<1$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
